Physical Education Activities
for Years 0–10

This resource provides a suggested list with examples of the games, physical
activities and sports as outlined in the Physical Education strand of Health
and Physical Education Years 0–10. This should be considered alongside the
Physical Education teaching sequence and associated guidance.

The intent of this resource is to provide a starting point for teachers to select a range of high-quality
movement experiences that support the knowledge and practices identified in the curriculum. The
suggested activities have been organised across the phases to illustrate the progression of
learning in Physical Education from Years 0–10.

The examples draw on a range of movement contexts, including sports, invasion games,
cooperative games, net/wall games, striking and fielding games, target games, challenge games,
outdoor education, and water safety activities. These provide opportunities for students to develop
movement capability, confidence, fitness, tactical awareness, cooperation, leadership, decision-
making, risk management, and enjoyment through participation in physical activity.

This is not an exhaustive list, and the example contexts are not mandated. They are examples.
Teachers know their learners, communities, and local contexts best, and may select alternative
activities that better reflect local environments, access to facilities and equipment, community
connections, student interests, teacher expertise, and the needs of their learners. Activities have
been grouped into those that require minimal equipment and those that require specialised
equipment or facilities. This reflects the range of contexts through which Physical Education is
taught.

This resource also reflects the increased emphasis on skill acquisition across Years 1–6. Students
learn and practise foundational movement skills, manipulative skills, game skills, and movement
strategies through a variety of activities and contexts. As students progress through the phases,
they use these skills with increasing confidence, precision, tactical awareness, and independence.




This resource builds on the MoveWell resource, which was developed through collaboration between Sport New
Zealand, Physical Education New Zealand, Accident Compensation Corporation, and is supported by the
Ministry of Education. For more information, please see: https://sportnz.org.nz/resources/movewell/.
